sc: Difficult delivery, cord pH 6.9, lethargic, hypotonic, seizures → Moderate HIE (Sarnat 2)
Lip smacking, cycling, apnoea that does not stop when the limb is held → Subtle seizure
Jittery infant of a diabetic mother at 2 hours → Hypoglycaemia
f: Cord pH < 7.0 · Apgar ≤ 5 at 10 min · encephalopathy · multi-organ injury
1 mild: hyperalert, jittery, normal by 24 h · 2 moderate: lethargic, hypotonia, seizures · 3 severe: coma, flaccid, absent reflexes
Supportive: ventilation, glucose, restrict fluids (SIADH, ATN), treat seizures · cooling to 33.5 °C for 72 h if ≥ 36 wk, moderate/severe, < 6 h
Commonest cause HIE · commonest type subtle · first test: blood glucose, then calcium, magnesium, sepsis
Phenobarbital first line · then phenytoin/levetiracetam · resistant: pyridoxine 100 mg IV · glucose or Ca 10% 2 ml/kg
Cerebral palsy (quadriplegic, dyskinetic) · epilepsy · deafness · best predictor: MRI in 1–2 weeks
trap: Jitteriness stops when the limb is held, a seizure does not · do not cool mild HIE · a febrile asphyxiated baby must be cooled to normal: fever worsens brain injury
